chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Some of our companions informed me from ʿĪṣ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, peace be upon him.
He said: When the deceased dies, then proceed with his preparation and hasten it. And when the deceased dies while in janabah, he is given one ghusl, then after that he is washed.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the first thing about these narrations is that their basis in all of them is ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, and he is one person, and it is not permissible for one individual to oppose a large group, as we have explained elsewhere. And even if it were sound, it could be understood as carrying a sense of recommendation rather than obligation and necessity. Moreover, it is possible that the point in these reports is that the command for ghusl after washing the deceased with the ghusl of janabah was in fact directed to the one washing him, as though it had been said to him: the deceased should be washed with the ghusl of janabah, then you yourself should perform ghusl. Thus, that may be an error from the narrator or the copyist, and this very narrator has himself narrated what we have mentioned.

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath associated with janabah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in al-Istibṣār regarding a person who dies while in janabah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling concerning a deceased person who dies while in janabah and mentions hastening the preparation of the deceased. It also includes a scholarly reconciliation explaining that the report does not conflict with stronger narrations, and that it may either indicate recommendation rather than obligation or reflect wording directed to the washer of the deceased.
